item.title: Naturalization of the canton of Valais: ordinary procedure
item.description: From residency to language test and integration: practical guide to ordinary naturalization in Valais, with deadlines, fees and step-by-step procedure.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal requirement: permit C + 10 years of continuous residence - Canton and municipalities add language test, integration and specific taxes - Procedures take on average 12-24 months from application to decree
## Key facts - **What**: Ordinary federal and cantonal naturalization - When: About 12-24 months from application - Where: Municipality of residence (application) → SEM Bern (federal decision) - Who: Vaud municipal authorities, Canton of Vaud, State Secretariat for Migration - Requirements: Permit C, 10 years residence, language/integration test
Naturalization in the Canton of Vaud is a process regulated at the federal level by the migration law and coordinated by the Vaud cantonal authorities. The legal basis is the residence permit of category C, valid for an unlimited duration.
### Fundamentals: the permit C and the 10 years of residence
The non-negotiable federal requirement is to have resided in Switzerland with a permit C for at least 10 consecutive years. It is not just any 10 years: the residence must be uninterrupted. Short absences (vacations, temporary stays abroad) are not counted as interruptions, but periods exceeding three consecutive months can extend the evaluation time of the application.
An important detail: years of previous residence with a permit B (short or medium-term stay) count double in the federal calculation. If a EU/EFTA citizen has resided 4 years with a permit B and subsequently 6 years with a permit C, the total calculation becomes 8 + 6 = 14 years, sufficient to submit an application. Furthermore, years between the ages of 8 and 18 are always counted double, regardless of the type of permit held.
For citizens of the European Union and EFTA countries (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway), the federal residence duration required is reduced to 5 years, a measure of reciprocity stipulated in the bilateral agreements Switzerland-EU.
### Linguistic and cultural integration: the cantonal tests
Vaud, like every Swiss canton, adds integration requirements beyond the federal residence criterion. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) coordinates at the national level, but each canton is competent for the language tests, civil integration and specific cultural requirements.
In Vaud, a test of knowledge of the French language, the official language of the canton, is required, with a level calibrated to the local integration needs. Some municipalities also accept Italian or German for residents in areas with linguistic minorities. The Vaud municipal authorities establish the specific evaluation criteria.
In addition, many Vaud municipalities require a civil and cultural integration test, which verifies basic knowledge of the Swiss democratic structure and civil coexistence in the canton. ## Practical implications: for those wishing to become a citizen of Valais The naturalization procedure in Valais is not immediate. From the submission of the application to the issuance of the federal decision, it is necessary to count on an average of 12-24 months. This period is not determined by a single authority: the Valais municipality proceeds with administrative checks (residence, criminal record), the Canton coordinates the process, and finally the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) in Bern issues the final federal decision.
### Realistic timelines and phases of the procedure
**Phase 1 (Municipality of residence)**: the applicant submits the application to the municipal office. The municipality collects documents (residence certificate, criminal record extract, proof of income if required), verifies the absence of criminal records or civil law conflicts, and organizes language and integration tests. This phase typically lasts 3-6 months.
Phase 2 (Canton of Valais): the file is transmitted to the competent cantonal authorities (cantonal naturalization/political rights office). The Canton examines the compatibility with cantonal law, collects any additional elements, and issues a recommendation. Timeline: 2-4 months.
Phase 3 (SEM - State Secretariat for Migration): the federal decision is pronounced based on residence, C permit, and compliance with federal requirements. Timeline: 1-3 months.
Totality of the process: from 6 to 13 months from the application to the final naturalization decree. Variations depend on: completeness of the initial documentation, any periods of incompleteness or requested clarifications, administrative workload of the municipality and the canton.
### Naturalization fees The naturalization involves fees that vary significantly by canton and municipality. In Valais, as in every canton, the municipalities set the fees for ordinary naturalization autonomously. These fees may depend on the applicant's income category, the composition of the family unit (when multiple people submit a joint application), and the specific policies of each Valais municipality.
It is not possible to indicate an exact amount without contacting the municipality of residence directly, but it is prudent to budget a wide range, sometimes adjusted to income according to local progressive criteria. The fees cover administrative checks, tests, and the processing of the application at the municipal and cantonal levels.
### Beyond naturalization: legal effects Once ordinary naturalization is obtained, the applicant becomes a Swiss citizen (and therefore also a citizen of Valais). They acquire the right to vote at the federal, cantonal, and municipal levels. Naturalization is an irrevocable act and produces immediate legal effects.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Step-by-step: how to submit the application in Valais
**1. Check federal prerequisites**: ensure you have had a C permit for at least 10 years (or a B permit which counts double), no irrevocable criminal record, and no unresolved civil debts of serious relevance. You can contact your municipality of residence for an informal pre-check.
2. Contact the municipal naturalization office: each municipality in Valais has an office or competent counter for naturalizations. Online, you can find the contact details and sometimes the preliminary application forms. Ask explicitly about the applicable taxes, the tests required (language, integration), and the required documentation.
3. Gather documentation: updated criminal record extract (not older than 3 months), official residence certificate, identity documents, income statements if required, and language proficiency certificates or diplomas already in possession.
4. Take the language and integration tests: the municipality organizes the dates and communicates the details. The tests vary by municipality but include language assessments (written and/or oral) and sometimes a civic-cultural test. No separate additional cost (included in the naturalization fees).
5. Submit the official application: fill out the official municipal form (available at the counter or online) and attach the complete documentation. Pay the required fees (the municipality indicates the payment methods).
6. Wait for processing and communications from the authorities: the municipality transmits the dossier to the canton, then to the SEM. You can ask for updates from the municipality, but the procedure cannot be expedited with external pressure. Once the federal decision is issued, the municipality officially communicates the result.
7. Registration of the completed naturalization: after the federal decree, you must register with the Civil Registry Office of the municipality to receive the naturalization certificate and access the rights of a citizen (registration on electoral lists, Swiss passport). This step is automatically managed by the municipal authorities.
### Essential documents for the application
- Ordinary naturalization application form (provided by the municipality) - Valid passport or identity document - Criminal record extract (not older than 3 months) - Official residence certificate - Bank account certificate (sometimes required) - Proof of language proficiency (if already in possession) - Any documents specifically requested by the municipality
### Official resources and next steps
The canton of Valais provides information on the official portal of the cantonal administration. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) publishes guidelines on federal ordinary naturalization on its institutional website.
The next step is to contact your municipality of residence in Valais directly to start the process. A visit to the municipal counter or a phone call to the competent offices is the safest way to obtain specific information about the required documentation, test dates, and fees applied by your municipality.
Do you want to check how your tax and social security rights and duties will change after Swiss naturalization? Consult our [calculator](nav:calculator) for a personalized estimate.

item.title: Aid to victims: 70 requests to the Beloved Foundation
item.description: The Beloved Foundation, established by the Canton of Valais, handled 70 requests for help. So far no refusal, you pay tens of thousands of francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Beloved Foundation receives 70 requests for assistance from victims in Crans-Montana - No requests refused so far, tens of thousands of CHF disbursed - Budget of 24 million CHF from Valais, Vaud, Crans-Montana and private donors - Psychological, educational and financial support interventions
## Key facts - **What**: Beloved Foundation for victims of the New Year's Eve fire - Where: Crans-Montana, Valais - When: Established on March 27 - Who: President Doris Leuthard (former federal councillor), director Christian Cardon - Budget: 24 million CHF in donations and pledges - Victims: 41 dead, 115 injured in the fire at Le Constellation bar - Requests: 70 received so far, no refusals
The Beloved Foundation, established by the Canton of Valais on March 27 to support the victims of the New Year's Eve fire at Le Constellation bar in Crans-Montana, has so far received around seventy requests for assistance. A positive note characterizes the first report: no request has been refused. This was reported by director Christian Cardon in an interview with Le Matin Dimanche, emphasizing that all requests receive careful and thorough evaluation. Some requests have already been approved and funded, while others are still under evaluation.
The foundation's overall budget is substantial: 24 million francs, coming from donations and pledges from the Canton of Valais, the Canton of Vaud, the Municipality of Crans-Montana, and private donors. A significant amount that demonstrates the commitment of multiple institutional levels in supporting the victims. So far, several tens of thousands of francs have been disbursed for concrete and direct interventions to the survivors and their families.
### The fire and the context of the foundation's establishment The fire at Le Constellation bar caused 41 deaths and 115 injuries, an extraordinarily serious tragedy that shook Valais and all of Switzerland. The Beloved Foundation was born from the initiative of the Canton of Valais as an integrated support tool to address the medium- and long-term consequences on victims, survivors, and their families.
According to director Cardon, the foundation's mandate is broad: it covers "rehabilitation interventions that will contribute to the recovery or reintegration of patients." A crucial aspect is that the foundation does not intend to duplicate the benefits provided by the Federal Law on Assistance to Victims of Crime (LAV), but rather to intervene "where there is a gap." This approach avoids bureaucratic duplications and focuses resources on unmet needs.
### Types of requests and support Many young people have turned to the foundation to receive help in the field of professional retraining. In other cases, parents of victims or people in financial difficulty as a result of the tragedy have presented specific projects for which the foundation has provided concrete support. The field of action is structured around three pillars: education, psychological support, and direct financial aid to families in difficulty.
The president of the foundation is the former federal councillor Doris Leuthard, who has emphasized that the tragedy will have lasting consequences on the survivors and their families. Her role ensures a federal vision and coordination with public institutions at multiple levels. ### How the Foundation Operates in the Context of Victim Support The Federal Law on Victim Assistance (LAV) provides basic services at the federal level, including psychological support, legal advice, and compensation for material damages. However, the needs generated by a tragedy like the one in Crans-Montana require a much broader and personalized intervention. The Beloved Foundation was created precisely to fill these specific gaps, working in synergy with the public network without duplicating services.
Among the interventions funded by the foundation are psychological rehabilitation and personalized emotional support, educational programs for children of victims with continued schooling and reorientation, professional requalification for affected youth, and direct economic aid to families in precarious situations. Cardon emphasized that the foundation operates in coordination with other public and private actors (hospitals, cantonal social services, non-profit organizations), not replacing but rather integrating ordinary services. This cooperative approach reduces the administrative burden on victims and ensures comprehensive care.
### Search for Additional Resources and Long-Term Support Despite the initial budget of 24 million francs, the foundation is already seeking additional funds. Leuthard explained that the needs will evolve and persist long-term, and the severity of the tragedy has generated traumas that will require years of continuous support. Cardon added concrete considerations: although the financial endowment is substantial, in the face of the psychological and physical consequences of the tragedy, the foundation will need additional resources to carry out its action over several years.
This reflects a broader reality of supporting victims in economic difficulty: the repair from mass tragedies is not a matter of one-time amounts, but of multi-year programs that respond to evolving needs over time. The foundation's initial estimates will need to be reassessed over time as new needs emerge: delayed returns to work, prolonged medical care, longer-term school support.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### How to request help from the Beloved Foundation Victims, survivors, and affected family members of the fire can submit requests for help to the Beloved Foundation. According to Cardon, the process is not rigid or bureaucratic: requests are examined on a case-by-case basis and evaluated based on the specific needs declared and documented. The director emphasized that so far there has been no negativity in the decisions, suggesting an inclusive approach and concrete support.
Requests are evaluated by a group of experts who verify the relevance of the intervention with respect to the foundation's criteria (education, psychological support, financial aid), the documentation of the link with the tragedy, and the economic situation and degree of need of the applicant. Decisions are not instantaneous: some requests have already been approved and funded with payments of several tens of thousands of francs, while others remain under evaluation. No precise timeline for the evaluations has been provided, but the fact that no request has been rejected so far suggests an inclusive attention to the process.
### Contacts, access, and complementarity with other benefits Specific contact details of the Beloved Foundation for submitting requests were not indicated in the official communication, but victims and family members can contact the municipal authorities of Crans-Montana or the Canton of Valais directly to obtain information on how to access support and complete the requests.
For those facing broader economic difficulties, in addition to the foundation's support, it is useful to check the available cantonal and municipal benefits: rent subsidies, health insurance premium reductions, education contributions, income support. Using the [calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate which benefits might be available based on your economic situation is a useful first step to identify additional resources. The Beloved Foundation represents a model of public-private intervention: the Canton of Valais has taken the first steps in coordinating a structured response, but the contribution of private donors and other cantons (Vaud) has been essential to create a truly significant and lasting support network over time.

## In brief - Swiss neutrality is at the center of a vote - Opponents see neutrality as an obstacle to EU integration - Neutrality allows economic diversification and international dialogue
## Key facts - **What**: Vote on the neutrality initiative - When: Not yet specified - Where: Switzerland - Who: Lorenzo Quadri, National Councillor of the Lega dei Ticinesi - Amount: Not applicable
Lorenzo Quadri, national councillor of the Lega dei Ticinesi, recently discussed the importance of Swiss neutrality. According to Quadri, neutrality is not a matter of right or left, but a fundamental pillar of the Swiss model. Neutrality has contributed to making Switzerland prosperous, safe, and open to the world. On September 27, Swiss citizens will be called upon to decide whether to continue with permanent and armed neutrality, which has allowed the country to diversify economic relations and make itself less blackmailable.
Opponents of the neutrality initiative are often those who would like to see Switzerland integrated into the European Union. Neutrality, in fact, represents an obstacle to submission to the EU. Quadri emphasizes that neutrality is one of the pillars of the Swiss model, along with direct democracy, federalism, independence, and the militia principle. Thanks to neutrality, Switzerland has become a privileged platform for international dialogue and mediation.
### Neutrality and the economy
Neutrality allows Switzerland to diversify economic relations, making the country less dependent on the EU. This is particularly important in a context of globalization, where diversification is a priority. Neutrality, however, must be consistent and not applied only when it is convenient. It is not an easy path: it requires a straight back and the ability to resist.
For this reason, it is absurd to accuse neutrality of meaning isolation. On the contrary, Switzerland is one of the most open countries in the world. Neutrality allows us to speak and relate economically with everyone, to mediate and to play a role that an aligned Switzerland would inevitably lose.
On September 27, Swiss citizens will decide whether to continue to determine their security policy autonomously or to delegate everything to Brussels and NATO. Neutrality, sovereignty, and independence go hand in hand. Giving up neutrality means calling into question the other two as well.
That is why, on September 27, a Yes to the neutrality initiative is needed. ### Practical implications of neutrality
Swiss neutrality has significant practical implications for the country's economy and politics.
